title: Every Possible UEFA Nations League Quarterfinal Ahead of Upcoming Draw
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray4:00 PM ESTSpain and France could collide again. / Matthew Visinsky/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesAudiences have already been spoiled by the caliber of UEFA Nations League action during the group stage, but the quality is only set to improve as the stakes are raised in next March’s quarterfinals.

The whole purpose of the Nations League was to rid European soccer of unnecessary friendlies and ensure teams regularly faced opponents on a similar level to themselves. The competition has aided the continent’s weaker teams, even providing unorthodox routes into major tournaments, but has also supplied an abundance of high-profile clashes in each of its five editions.
League A has been the battleground for the collision of behemoths, as evidenced by the most recent group stage with fixtures such as Spain vs. England and France vs. Italy.

The 2026–27 group stage has now concluded, with eight nations booking their ticket to the quarterfinals. Friday’s draw will determine the exact fixtures on the docket during the next international break, but they will be unquestionably tantalizing considering the quality of countries entering the knockout stage.
Here is every quarterfinalist’s possible opponents for the next round.

France is under new management for the current Nations League campaign. / Xavier Laine/Getty ImagesPossible Opponents: Netherlands, Spain or Norway

Zinédine Zidane’s start as France manager was perfectly pleasant. While the two-time world champion never reached the peak of its power, even losing 3–1 away at Italy, it secured top spot in Group A3 without ever truly breaking stride.

An arduous battle awaits in the quarterfinal, however, with revenge potentially on the cards in a repeat of the 2026 World Cup semifinal with Spain. Les Bleus were comfortably beaten when the nations clashed in North America, and they would ideally want to avoid Luis de la Fuente’s well-oiled machine.

Battles with the Netherlands or Norway are more appetizing, with the latter conquered by France during the World Cup group stage. It has won seven of its last nine games against the Dutch across all competitions.
Germany is beginning to find its feet under Jürgen Klopp (right). / Tom Weller/picture alliance/Getty ImagesPossible Opponents: Belgium, Spain or Norway

Jürgen Klopp’s first six matches as Germany boss were a mixed bag. Greece proved his kryptonite in Group A2, but convincing wins over Serbia and the 5–0 thrashing of the Netherlands on Matchday 6 ensured the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund manager guided Die Mannschaft to first place.

One would expect Germany’s upward trajectory to continue as Klopp’s reign progresses, and a meeting with world champion Spain would certainly prove the acid test. It hasn’t beaten La Roja in a competitive fixture since Euro ‘88.

Norway would be another awkward competitor, especially following last summer’s World Cup performance from Ståke Solbakken’s side, while Mark van Bommel’s Belgium proved tricky customers for France and Italy during the group stage.
England is flying high right now. / Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesPossible Opponents: Belgium, Netherlands or Norway

England’s confidence could hardly be higher. Not only does it now officially boast the world’s best player, Ballon d’Or-winning captain Harry Kane, it recently ended Spain’s 43-match unbeaten run in regulation time to clinch first place in Group A3.

Luckily for Thomas Tuchel’s men, they can’t face Spain again in the last eight due to UEFA’s regulations for the draw, but they could play a repeat of their World Cup quarterfinal with Norway, which only narrowly ended in their favor after extra time and some Jude Bellingham brilliance.

Supporters will be greeted by plenty of familiar faces if the Three Lions are drawn against the Netherlands, who fielded nine current and former Premier League players in their most recent starting XI. Belgium also boasts an arsenal of talent which has ties with English soccer, including the likes of Kevin De Bruyne, Romelu Lukaku, Youri Tielemans and Jérémy Doku.
Portugal is enjoying life without Cristiano Ronaldo. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesPossible Opponents: Belgium, Netherlands or Spain

Even without international soccer’s greatest goalscorer for much of the group stage, Portugal eased to top spot in Group A4. The current Nations League holder marched to five wins from six as it bid an underwhelming farewell to Cristiano Ronaldo.
